extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors in mathematical logic preparing submissions to The Journal of Symbolic Logic
extracted.subtask_description: Author instructions for submitting research manuscripts to The Journal of Symbolic Logic, describing subject scope, expected novelty and audience, and procedural submission notes. Targets researchers preparing materials and using the journal's submission system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject scope / topical fit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journal of Symbolic Logic publishes research in mathematical logic and its applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be within mathematical logic or its applications; content outside this scope is unlikely to be appropriate for the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are expected to exhibit innovation and not merely be minor variations on established work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should present novel contributions rather than small variations; the journal seeks work that advances the field intellectually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest to a broad audience
rubrics_metrics.description: They should also be of interest to a broad audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for results and presentations that appeal beyond an extremely narrow sub-specialty within logic; clarity and significance for a wider community are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall quality and rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journal of Symbolic Logic publishes research ... of the highest quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are held to high standards of exposition, correctness, and significance; the journal's prestige 'derives from ... the standard of submissions -- which, combined with the standards of reviewing' and thus authors should ensure rigorous proofs and clear exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission system account requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You will need an account for the submission system, which is separate to your Cambridge Core account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must create/login to the partner submission system; for login and submission support, visit the submission and support pages. Review the journal's 'preparing your materials' page before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access / APC waiver and coverage notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain article types (for example, Research Articles) may be eligible for APC waivers or discounts under one of the agreements Cambridge University Press has made to support open access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each research article accepted by the Journal, if published Gold Open Access, all or part of the publication costs may be covered by agreements; authors should consult the journal's open access/APC information for eligibility and coverage details.
